summary: Don't-trust-verify pass per operator. Re-grounded in CLAUDE.md + CLAUDE_ROOT.md; re-ran all four root gates and tapit-attest tests fresh — all green honestly. Adversarial review of the Phase 2.5 surface surfaced two real correctness bugs and fixed both. First bug: createJournalEntry, JournalCard, JournalDetail all computed the entry's digest as sha256(JSON.stringify(att)) instead of tapit-attest's canonical envelopeId(att). This broke determinism across JS engines (JSON.stringify property order is implementation-defined for non-integer keys), broke OTS commit semantics (the proof should commit to the digest signatures bind to), and broke URL stability across added signatures (Phase 2.6 witness co-signing would have changed every existing entry's URL). Fix: import envelopeId from tapit-attest and use it in all three sites. Second bug: confirmed OTS anchors lived in the IDB queue but never got attached to the held attestation, so the encrypted wallet snapshot (which is what backup/restore uses) had no Bitcoin block heights. A user restoring from backup would lose every Time-verified · block N badge they had earned. Fix: WalletProvider subscribes to the anchor worker, on each confirmed state it finds the matching held attestation by envelopeId, calls wallet.hold() with the anchor attached (replaces by id since envelopeId is anchor-independent), and debounces a 2-second save so a flood of confirmations on app reopen produces one PBKDF2 cycle.
